title: Composition and strict base change in logarithmic smoothness
statement: For locally Noetherian fs log schemes [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], use log smooth and log etale in the chart sense of [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale]. Composites of log smooth morphisms are log smooth; log etale morphisms are log smooth; hence a log etale morphism followed by a log smooth morphism is log smooth. A strict base change of a log smooth morphism is log smooth, where strict means the source log structure is the log structure pulled back from the target. These properties can be checked on jointly surjective strict etale neighborhoods of source and target. For a nonempty coherent log ideal on an fs log scheme, its saturated log blowup, whenever it exists, is log etale. Finite saturated log blowup towers are therefore log etale.

source.place: VI 1.1--1.7 and 2.1--2.2; VIII 3.3.7--3.3.10 (saturated log blowup charts); X proof of 1.1, 1.3 and 1.8, pp.139,146--148. Chart properties used explicitly there; general log-smooth chart calculus is Kato 1988 Theorem 3.5, WANTED locally.

from.place: Proof Step 3: dimension-normalized Verdier duality, regular finite-torsion local model; pointwise purity and composition used to compare the normalized curve with the ambient regular scheme. Input: Gabber purity for a regular Noetherian closed pair. More precisely: Expose XVI, section 3.7 second paragraph through its last paragraph, printed pp.254--255: semistable G-alteration, ell-Sylow H, tame equivariant modification, quotient over T=S prime/H, and log resolution. Geometric construction only, before applying Theorem 3.6.2 and Proposition 3.5.7; preliminary finite extension to normalize constants in the first paragraph. Specifically: XVI 3.7: equivariant modification X double-prime and log-smooth quotient X double-prime/H. Supporting construction and local calculations in ILO VIII 4--5 and X 1.2--1.8.
